coaching.title: Active Recovery Day
coaching.message: Week 2 of the vert block opens with recovery, not volume. Keep the 2-mile shakeout truly easy — Zone 1, ~120-135 bpm, fully conversational, feet quiet. Pair it with Strength Session 1: single-leg work, hips, core, and controlled step-downs to bank eccentric strength for the Julian Alps descents. No hard running today; if the legs feel heavy from yesterday's 1,200 ft hill session, cut the jog and just walk and mobilize. The adaptation from this week's climbing happens now.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Recovery day, so anchor around ~220g carbs across the day to refill glycogen after yesterday's vert. Front-load protein — aim 30-40g per meal (~1.6-2 g/kg total) to drive repair from the step-down eccentric loading. Lean on anti-inflammatory foods (berries, leafy greens, olive oil, oily fish) and stay ahead on fluids and sodium in the San Salvador heat. No race-fueling needed today since there's no long session.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: This is the recovery cue for the whole week — treat it seriously. After strength, spend 8-10 min on hips, calves, and ankles plus light foam rolling on quads and glutes to prep the descending muscles. Legs up the wall for 5 minutes if you've been in transit. Protect sleep tonight — 7.5-9 hours is where the vert block actually pays off.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: 45 days to Kranjska Gora and you're in the Peak Phase — the temptation is to add more. Resist it. Taking the easy day as prescribed is a decision a disciplined athlete makes, not a session you skipped. The Julian Alps 50K is won on well-executed recovery weeks that let the hard vert stick. Bank the discipline today; spend it on the climbs in September.
